scope: System invariants already enforced by the current AtM baseline; future v1 invariants are added by the PR that implements them.

invariants.statement: Startup qualification must fail closed when the Flatpak application/runtime identity required by the current qualification policy cannot be established.
Invalid persisted repository state must not be overwritten or repaired implicitly by normal repository-state mutations.

A persisted repository snapshot may be reported ready only when the snapshot path is bound to the persisted SHA, manifest identity validates, the repository version matches, and the retrieval index is valid or is rebuilt from that same snapshot.
A repository snapshot whose integrity seal no longer matches its contents must not remain usable as ready current state.
Repository archive ingestion must enforce bounded extraction and reject unsafe paths or link-like archive entries before a snapshot can be promoted.
A retrieval index may be reused only when it validates against the exact repository and snapshot sources; an invalid derived index must be rejected and rebuilt or surface an error.
A conversation session may start only from frozen grounding and must keep the selected AI model identity, including its digest when available, pinned until the session is reset.
The same logical evidence object must expose the same structured semantic metadata regardless of whether it is discovered by exact, lexical, or tabular retrieval.

Only an explicit frozen AtM scientific profile rule matching the evidence repository and structural selector may produce TYPED_VALIDATED; repository payload text cannot grant itself scientific authority.
Textual, unsupported, provenance-incomplete, or profile-recognized malformed evidence must fail closed as a non-typed scientific classification and must never be silently promoted to TYPED_VALIDATED.

The EWD, CBD, and RMD v1 production profile factories are deny-by-default allowlists: only explicitly declared structural selectors and exact dataset logical source IDs may be recognized, and unlisted or near-match evidence remains unsupported.

Scientific control evidence must be read only through AtM-owned fixed repository/path/JSON-Pointer/type specifications from the pinned snapshot, without retrieval or textual fallback; unsafe paths, symlink traversal, unresolved pointers and type mismatches must fail closed.

SCI-04 must keep ScientificContentId, QualifiedArtifactId, and StorageDigest distinct: semantic content is canonically identified independently of storage/provenance, qualification binds that content to pinned provenance and semantic-profile identity, and storage digest covers the complete stored artifact; only TYPED_VALIDATED evidence or recognized deterministic controls may enter the artifact layer, and mutation or incomplete provenance must fail validation.

SCI-05 scientific results must be finalized deterministically from established typed facts and deterministic constraints: support provenance, including exact per-fact/per-constraint/per-conflict bindings, belongs to QualifiedArtifactId rather than ScientificContentId; qualification support sets may admit only SCI-04 artifacts that pass canonical artifact validation and match the expected evidence/control kind, all support IDs must be qualified, retrieval order must not affect result identities, duplicate semantic record IDs must fail closed, and Gold Set v0 must pass all seven pinned non-derived cases without an LLM or network; SCI-06 derivation admission is governed separately by later invariants.

Scientific executable transformations are deny-by-default: only versioned operations compiled into the AtM Scientific Operation Registry may execute; repository equations, formula strings, LLM output and arbitrary user code are not executable authority. Registered operations must enforce fixed input roles, finite numeric inputs, explicit unit rules and operation-specific preconditions, and undefined safe-ratio results must remain explicit missing values rather than being forced to zero.

SRA derived facts may be created only by deterministic re-execution of registered DERIVATION operations over explicitly role-bound established facts: input values and units must come from qualified established facts, inherited support must equal the exact union of input support, the SRA numeric policy must explicitly authorize the operation numeric profile, operation/profile/repository qualification must be present, operation claims must exactly match used derivations, and output value, binary64 bits, missing-state reason and input bindings must validate against re-execution; CHECK operations remain inadmissible as derived facts until a versioned constraint/tolerance policy is bound.

Scientific presentation may be created only from a finalized SRA that still passes deterministic validation. SCI-07a RealizationView must preserve every answerability, established-fact, derived-fact, constraint, conflict and limitation block as mandatory; Direct Render must emit every mandatory block exactly once, preserve scientific values, units, status/reason codes and operation identities verbatim, derive support metadata only from SRA support, escape control characters, and have no LLM dependency.

The AtM SQLite Control State foundation must accept only the AtM application ID and supported schema version, run with foreign keys enabled, WAL journaling and FULL synchronous durability, validate required schema/integrity/foreign keys, fail closed for foreign, newer, corrupt or incomplete databases, and remain shadow-only without reading or mutating repository-state.json.

Legacy repository-state import must accept only the same validated v1/v2 repository semantics as RepositoryStateStore, preserve SHA/version/seal values exactly, reject duplicates and unknown repositories, write a fresh inactive Control DB generation atomically and in deterministic repository-id order, verify semantic equivalence before marking the generation COMPLETE, roll back on any failure, refuse replacement of an existing generation, leave active_state unset, and never mutate repository-state.json; the import path remains dormant until the separately qualified cutover.

The STATE-03a cutover primitive may publish control-state.sqlite3 only when that authoritative path is absent. It must validate legacy state before candidate creation, build and fully validate the candidate privately in the same state directory, import and semantically verify legacy state when present, activate only the verified COMPLETE generation, record cutover provenance, checkpoint and close WAL cleanly, fsync the database, publish without replacing a concurrent/existing authority, fsync the directory, leave repository-state.json byte-for-byte untouched, and remove unpublished candidates on failure. STATE-03a remains runtime-dormant and does not itself switch application authority.

The DB-backed repository-state adapter must read only a valid existing AtM Control DB and only its active COMPLETE generation, must never fall back to repository-state.json or implicitly create a missing authority, must preserve repository SHA/version/seal validation, must apply set_current and set_snapshot_seal transactionally to the active authority, must create the first active generation only inside an already-published empty Control DB, and must restore its in-memory record when persistence fails. The adapter remains unwired from application startup and repository lifecycle until a separate authority-switch gate.

After the STATE-03 authority switch, an existing control-state.sqlite3 is the sole repository-state authority: a valid DB must win regardless of legacy JSON contents, an invalid existing DB must fail closed without JSON fallback, and JSON migration is permitted only when the DB is absent. Startup qualification must reconcile and enroll seals through the Control DB, repository-state invalidity must block installation qualification, RepositoryLifecycleService must operate only on reloaded valid Control DB state, and normal production operations must not write repository-state.json.

Normal Control DB repository-state mutations must be copy-on-write: set_current and set_snapshot_seal must never update a previously COMPLETE generation, must create a fresh CANDIDATE from the exact active COMPLETE generation inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, apply the mutation only to the candidate, mark it COMPLETE, atomically advance active_state with an expected-previous-generation guard, and roll back the entire candidate on any failure so no partial or orphan CANDIDATE state remains.
